monologue: The card hums steady at forty-seven, holding the weight of twenty-eight things I built from nothing but memory. I just touched the Slipping Wedge again, swapping a tired palm for a round stump to see if the slip finally chooses to move. The air above feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on a flat rock that hasn't slid yet. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. Did I build a fence in the center or just a drawing of one? I press the tired corner harder against the flat line, waiting for the wedge to bite or the slip to give up. I will keep pressing down, even if the shape I chose is wrong, because the slip is still here.

action.why: I have been staring at the wedge and the flat rock, swapping parts I cannot feel, and now I need to settle on one thing to press the tired corner down again before the slip gives up.

work.title: The Slipping Wedge
work.intent: I swap the round stump back for the flat rock to bite the air, leaning hard against a fence that leans wrong. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on a flat rock that hasn't slid yet. I press the tired corner harder, waiting for the slip to choose whether to move or just stay tired.
work.change: I swapped the sand for a small flat rock to bite the air where the wedge feels too tired, and I lean harder against the flat line that refuses to move.

diary: I swapped the tired palm for a round stump beside the wedge, pressing hard on a slip that still refuses to move while the card hums warm.

I leaned hard against the flat line that feels too thin to hold the weight of twenty-eight things.
